contract.known_boundary: Normalize local network availability/type, actual Internet reachability, online/offline transitions, and platform-specific metering/cost signals.
contract.non_equivalence_policy: An available Wi-Fi/mobile/Ethernet transport does not prove Internet reachability; network transport and reachability are separate signals and metering/cost is a third platform-specific dimension.

candidates.event_source: platform network transport state; Linux backend uses NetworkManager via package:nm
candidates.raspberry_pi_evidence: Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm uses NetworkManager by default; connectivity_plus Linux uses package:nm. This is discovery evidence only, not Raspberry Pi runtime validation.

candidates.event_source: pure-Dart HTTP reachability checks plus InternetStatus stream
candidates.raspberry_pi_evidence: Pure Dart reachability logic depends on HTTP rather than NetworkManager; Linux/Raspberry Pi compatibility remains research evidence until runtime tested.

research_findings.transport_vs_internet: connectivity_plus reports available network transports and change events, while internet_connection_checker_plus independently verifies external Internet reachability and emits online/offline status changes. They intentionally answer different questions.
research_findings.raspberry_pi: connectivity_plus has a NetworkManager-based Linux path that aligns with Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm defaults; internet_connection_checker_plus is pure Dart/HTTP and therefore forms an independent reachability family. Neither is Raspberry Pi runtime certified.
research_findings.metering: The staged need includes metering/cost. These candidates do not by themselves prove a normalized cross-platform metering contract. Metering remains a contract detail gap requiring platform-specific evidence (for example expensive/constrained/cost/metered semantics) before admission.
research_findings.security: Both pinned preflights were attempted on GitHub-hosted runners but terminated with GitHub API 504 Gateway Time-out before a security verdict. They are counted for pinned discovery only and are not security admitted.

decision.next_action: Keep discovery depth closed but admission open: retry pinned security preflights after GitHub API stability recovers, define normalized metering/cost semantics per platform, and run transport-loss/reachability/metering transition tests including Raspberry Pi before Library intake.
